blocker.summary: The r399-r431 investigation chain is CLOSED (allocator, shutdown hang, presentation all fixed/live-verified), and r432 fixed a real double-present regression in r430's fix (caught only by a truly clean rebuild) while discovering the native/ uncommitted backlog is far wider than r424 had characterized as 'the Vulkan backlog'. r433 catalogued that wider backlog precisely rather than committing it: 20 uncommitted paths under native/, split into 14 git-tracked files with a delta against HEAD and 6 never-committed files. The dominant fact: native_vulkan_backend.cpp (+2881/-0 of 3015 lines) and native_xenos_tests.cpp (+3825/-16 of 4241 lines) are almost entirely uncommitted -- their last HEAD commit (e0afccdd, 2026-08-31, itself a prior backlog catch-up for r2-r76) is an early skeleton. This is not speculative work: it is the actual native rendering engine (Vulkan backend/device, pinned shaders, shader translator) and its test suite, which ctest has exercised and passed on every cycle since r413, including r432's clean-rebuild ctest 11/11. Report grep shows this backlog is continuous since r94, not recent. A precedent for a bundled catch-up commit of exactly this shape already exists in this repo's own history (e0afccdd). Explicit decision this cycle: do NOT commit it -- catalogue only, per the same standing-decision-stays-with-the-user stance repeated since r423. Named for r434, conditional on the user: decide whether/how to commit this catalogued backlog (one bundled catch-up commit vs. per-subsystem), or continue elsewhere (real present pixel content, or the already-known-and-disposed-of Vulkan scratch file). Nothing in this catalogue changed any source file; gates and ctest are unaffected from r432's state.
